summary: CMMC C3PAOs by State: Cyber AB Directory Snapshot: scope, evidence, limitations, and the decisions buyers need to make.
body_markdown:
For implementation support, review[vCISO support for government contractors](https://getagency.com/vciso-for-government-contractors?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=cmmc&utm_content=cmmc-c3paos-by-state__in_text) and[CMMC certification timing](https://getagency.com/questions/how-long-does-cmmc-certification-take?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=cmmc&utm_content=cmmc-c3paos-by-state__in_text) . Confirm scope and operating responsibilities before choosing an engagement.


## What does the directory count represent?


Agency retrieved the C3PAO role results from the[Cyber AB Marketplace](https://cyberab.org/Catalog) and checked the returned listing records. The analysis includes active records marked in good standing. It counts directory organizations rather than assessors, assessment slots, or completions.


The current[CMMC policy](https://dodcio.defense.gov/CMMC/Policy/) must be checked separately. A directory count does not establish a contractor deadline or the assessment required under a particular contract.


## How are C3PAOs assigned to a state?


Each retained record uses the region of its primary contact address. Organizations with a non-US primary address are grouped separately. Regions supported by a provider are not substituted for office locations, because doing so would count the same organization repeatedly across states.


Use the accessible table or CSV for the complete regional breakdown. A state’s count does not measure whether providers will travel, work remotely, or have experience with your system.
